classes.name: Nimitz class
classes.summary: U.S. nuclear-powered aircraft carriers combining a large aviation deck, steam catapults and arrested recovery to operate an embarked carrier air wing.

sections.title: Flight deck and aviation facilities
sections.text: NAVSEA’s 2020 comparison describes a 4.5-acre flight deck, three hangar bays and four aircraft elevators. These are class reference features; individual ships have received different modernization work during their service lives.

sections.title: Steam catapult launch
sections.text: Steam pressure drives pistons connected to the catapult shuttle, accelerating the attached aircraft along the launch track. Nimitz-class ships have four steam catapults.

sections.title: Arrested recovery
sections.text: The Naval Air Systems Command (NAVAIR) identifies the Mark-7 (Mk-7) Mod 3 and Mod 4 as Nimitz-class arresting-gear designs. The class uses arrested recovery for its carrier fixed-wing aircraft.

sections.title: Air wing roles
sections.text: The Navy’s 2017 carrier-strike-group instruction groups air-wing capabilities into strike fighters, airborne early warning, electronic warfare and helicopters. Helicopter roles include search and rescue, logistics, surface warfare and anti-submarine warfare. These role categories describe the breadth of aviation support; they do not fix a ship’s embarked aircraft mix in 2026.

classes.name: Gerald R. Ford class
classes.summary: Nuclear-powered fleet carriers that replace steam catapults with electromagnetic launch and use a new digitally controlled arresting system. The lead ship introduced the systems at sea before its first deployment.

facts.label: Builder
facts.value: HII Newport News Shipbuilding, Virginia, United States

facts.label: Propulsion
facts.value: Two nuclear reactors driving four shafts

facts.label: Lead-ship length
facts.value: About 337 m (1,106 ft), using CVN-78 command-history figures

facts.label: Lead-ship flight-deck width
facts.value: About 78 m (256 ft)

facts.label: Full-load displacement
facts.value: Approximately 101,600 tonnes (100,000 long tons), published for CVN-78

facts.label: Published speed
facts.value: More than 30 kn, as published in the CVN-78 command history

facts.label: Published complement
facts.value: 4,539 including ship, air wing and staff in the Ford media kit; a reference figure rather than a live crew count

facts.label: Published aircraft figure
facts.value: 75+ in the Ford media kit; an air-wing reference figure, not a guaranteed embarkation or fixed maximum

facts.label: Aircraft elevators
facts.value: Three between hangar and flight deck; Nimitz-class ships have four

facts.label: Weapons elevators
facts.value: Eleven Advanced Weapons Elevators on CVN-78

facts.label: Launch system
facts.value: Electromagnetic Aircraft Launch System (EMALS)

facts.label: Recovery system
facts.value: Advanced Arresting Gear (AAG)

sections.title: Launch and recovery
sections.text: The Electromagnetic Aircraft Launch System (EMALS) converts stored kinetic energy into electrically controlled catapult launch power. Advanced Arresting Gear (AAG) uses energy absorbers, power conditioning and digital controls to arrest landing aircraft. The Naval Air Systems Command (NAVAIR) describes both systems as designed to support a broad range of aircraft.

sections.title: Flight deck and logistics
sections.text: The Ford design uses three aircraft elevators rather than Nimitz’s four. Separate Advanced Weapons Elevators move ordnance towards the flight deck using electromagnetic motors. All eleven weapons elevators on Gerald R. Ford had been turned over to the crew by 22 December 2021.

sections.title: Air wing and roles
sections.text: The ship supports a mixed carrier air wing. During 2022 workups, Carrier Air Wing 8 (CVW-8) operated Super Hornets, Hawkeyes, Growlers and MH-60R/S helicopters from Ford. Its inaugural deployment combined Atlantic operations with allied training. This is a dated example of the air wing’s aviation roles; the aircraft mix varies between deployments.

sections.title: Differences within the class
sections.text: Radar fit differs within the class. Gerald R. Ford was built with Dual Band Radar; the Navy specified Enterprise Air Surveillance Radar for John F. Kennedy. The dimensions and complement figures above identify the lead-ship or published reference baseline to which they apply.

overview.text: The class namesake entered service in 1975. Its career includes Arabian Sea operations supporting tanker protection and a later role in introducing the F-35C to carrier operations.

milestones.text: Keel laid at Newport News.
Commissioned at Naval Station Norfolk.
Began North Arabian Sea operations in October supporting Operation Earnest Will.
Hosted the F-35C’s first arrested landing aboard an aircraft carrier during developmental testing.

overview.text: The second Nimitz-class carrier entered service in 1977. Beyond carrier air operations, Eisenhower demonstrated a joint transport role by embarking Army forces for the 1994 intervention in Haiti.

milestones.text: Commissioned under Capt. William E. Ramsey.
Operated in the Red Sea following Iraq’s invasion of Kuwait, including maritime interception supporting the United Nations embargo.
In September, embarked soldiers and equipment of the Army’s 10th Mountain Division for Operation Uphold Democracy off Haiti.
Began its midlife refueling and complex overhaul at Newport News; returned to Naval Station Norfolk on 25 January 2005.

overview.text: Commissioned in 1982 as the third Nimitz-class carrier, Carl Vinson has served in humanitarian relief as well as aviation deployments, including the 2021 introduction of F-35C and CMV-22B aircraft to an operational carrier-strike-group deployment.

milestones.text: Commissioned at Newport News after more than seven years of construction.
Supported the Haiti earthquake response as part of Operation Unified Response.
Departed San Diego with the first carrier-strike-group deployment to include both F-35C Lightning II and CMV-22B Osprey aircraft.

overview.text: Theodore Roosevelt entered service in 1986 and flew combat strikes during Desert Storm in 1991. Its 2013 redelivery followed a midlife overhaul covering reactor refueling and modernization of propulsion, combat and aviation support systems.

milestones.text: Commissioned with Capt. Paul W. Parcells as its first commanding officer.
Entered the Persian Gulf and launched its first combat strike of Operation Desert Storm that evening.
Redelivered to the Navy after successful sea trials concluding its refueling and complex overhaul.

overview.text: Abraham Lincoln’s early service paired carrier air operations with disaster response: it supported evacuation after Mount Pinatubo’s eruption on its first deployment and later delivered aid after the 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami.

milestones.text: Commissioned at Norfolk, Virginia.
Diverted during its maiden deployment to support Operation Fiery Vigil evacuations after Mount Pinatubo erupted in the Philippines.
Diverted after the December tsunami to Operation Unified Assistance, delivering supplies and aid in Southeast Asia before returning in March 2005.
Redelivered to the Navy after sea trials, completing the refueling and complex overhaul that began in March 2013.

overview.text: George Washington combined post-September 11 air-defense and combat-support deployments with a pioneering role as the first nuclear-powered carrier forward-deployed to Japan in 2008. Its midlife refueling and complex overhaul concluded in May 2023.

milestones.text: In September, deployed to New York City to provide air defense after the September 11 attacks.
Became the first nuclear-powered aircraft carrier forward-deployed to Japan. A fire during its transfer voyage required repairs in San Diego.
Entered refueling and complex overhaul at Newport News Shipbuilding.
Completed its refueling and complex overhaul and was redelivered to the Navy after sea trials.

overview.text: John C. Stennis began its deployment career with a Persian Gulf voyage in 1998 and subsequently supported combat operations in Afghanistan. Its midlife refueling and complex overhaul began in 2021; undocking in April 2024 marked a transition to further installation and testing at an outfitting berth.

milestones.text: Departed on its first deployment to the Persian Gulf.
Deployed with Carrier Air Wing Nine for combat operations over Afghanistan in support of Operation Enduring Freedom, two months earlier than planned.
Transited from Norfolk to Newport News Shipbuilding to begin refueling and complex overhaul.
Left dry dock and moved to an outfitting berth for the next phase of refueling and complex overhaul.

overview.text: Harry S. Truman supported Southern Watch on its first deployment, launched combat missions over Iraq in 2003 and served as a helicopter relief platform after Hurricane Katrina. The ship also hosted early carrier trials of the E-2D Advanced Hawkeye.

milestones.text: Departed on its maiden deployment; its embarked air wing supported Operation Southern Watch before the ship returned in May 2001.
Its air wing launched its first Operation Iraqi Freedom combat missions from the eastern Mediterranean.
In September, embarked detachments from 13 helicopter squadrons and served as Joint Task Force Gulf Coast flagship during Hurricane Katrina relief.
In February, hosted the E-2D Advanced Hawkeye’s first carrier takeoff.

overview.text: Ronald Reagan reached the Pacific by sailing around South America in 2004, then began combat-support deployments in 2006. Its 2011 Operation Tomodachi work included helicopter refueling and relief support after Japan’s earthquake and tsunami; in 2015 it began the journey to take over the forward-deployed carrier role.

milestones.text: Departed Norfolk on a voyage around South America to its new San Diego homeport.
Departed San Diego on its maiden deployment, supporting Operations Iraqi Freedom and Enduring Freedom.
In March, arrived off eastern Honshu as a helicopter refueling platform for rescue and recovery following Japan’s earthquake and tsunami.
Departed for the U.S. 7th Fleet area to assume the forward-deployed aircraft carrier role.

overview.text: George H.W. Bush supported Operations Enduring Freedom and New Dawn during its first deployment in 2011. In 2013 it became a major test platform for unmanned carrier aviation, hosting the X-47B demonstrator’s first carrier catapult launch and arrested landing.

milestones.text: Began its maiden deployment, supporting Operations Enduring Freedom and New Dawn and taking part in Exercise Saxon Warrior.
Began a planned incremental availability at Norfolk Naval Shipyard for technical upgrades.
Hosted the X-47B demonstrator’s first catapult launch from an aircraft carrier at sea.
Hosted the first arrested landing by an unmanned aircraft aboard a modern aircraft carrier, using the X-47B demonstrator.

overview.text: The lead Ford-class ship was both a fleet carrier and the first seagoing installation of its new launch and arresting systems. Its post-commissioning programme progressed through first fixed-wing flight operations, shock trials and completion of weapons elevators before the inaugural Atlantic deployment in 2022.

milestones.text: Keel laid at Newport News in November.
Christened at Newport News.
Commissioned as USS Gerald R. Ford (CVN-78).
An F/A-18F from Air Test and Evaluation Squadron 23 (VX-23) made the first arrested landing and catapult launch aboard the ship, using AAG and EMALS.
Completed Full Ship Shock Trials with the third explosive event of the series.
The eleventh and final Advanced Weapons Elevator was turned over to the crew.
Departed Norfolk for its first deployment, with Carrier Air Wing 8 (CVW-8) for Atlantic training alongside allies and partners.
Returned from its inaugural Atlantic deployment after exercises and port visits with allies and partners.
